source.title: Estimating Example Difficulty using Variance of Gradients
source.authors: Chirag Agarwal; Daniel D'Souza; Sara Hooker

record.file_problem: The supplied text contains the full paper and appendix; no garbling or cutoff noted.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests training with 20% randomly shuffled labels and reports zero training error, a related but narrower label-noise condition than the claim’s fully random labeling setting.
record.gate_note: The paper reports zero training error after replacing 20% of labels with randomly shuffled labels. Its VoG comparisons between shuffled-label and correct-label examples are results about the proposed difficulty score, not about the claim versions’ learning behavior.
record.test_reason: Section 4.1 repeats the original label-corruption experiment using standard network training and training error as the measure. Its own zero-error result tests the perfect-training-fit component of V4 at 20% corruption.
record.authors_conclusion: The record accurately summarizes the noisy-label experiment: the network reaches zero training error with 20% shuffled labels, and VoG distinguishes shuffled-label examples. The paper's broader conclusion is that VoG efficiently ranks example difficulty for auditing and out-of-distribution detection, including using predicted labels.
record.recipe_differences: The paper says it replicates the general experiment setup of Zhang et al. and changes 20% of labels; it does not test the original study’s full random-label condition or its training-time comparison.

fits_no_version.finding: Shuffled-label examples have higher mean VoG than correctly labeled examples on both datasets, with p < 0.001.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VoG distinguishes examples assigned shuffled labels from correctly labeled examples under 20% label shuffling.

fits_no_version.finding: The association between VoG rank and test error reverses between early and late training; the CIFAR early-stage result requires a lower learning rate.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: VoG's relationship to example difficulty depends on training stage and, for the reported CIFAR results, learning rate.

record.problems: The noisy-label experiment tests only 20% corruption, and the supplied results do not report test error or training time for this experiment.

untested.parts: Completely random labeling, chance test performance, and fitting without changing architecture or training hyperparameters.
Relative training time and convergence speed across corruption fractions.
Training to zero error on shuffled pixels, independently permuted pixels, or Gaussian-noise inputs. Gaussian inputs here are used for out-of-distribution detection.
Corruption fractions other than 20%, continued perfect fitting across a corruption sweep, and steadily increasing test error toward chance.
Whether explicit regularizers prevent fully random-label fitting and whether removing them preserves true-label generalization.
Direct comparison of when real-label patterns and noisy labels are learned. Early/late VoG analyses do not establish that ordering.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source. Its primary purpose is evaluating VoG, but its explicitly reported training-error result independently bears on V4. Unmeasured corruption levels and test-error trends are untested, not evidence limiting scope.

versions.untested_parts: The paper tests 20% shuffled labels, not a completely random labeling of the training set; it does not report test error at chance.
No comparison of training time or convergence speed across label-noise fractions.
No shuffled-pixel, independently permuted-pixel, or Gaussian-noise input training results.
Only the 20% shuffled-label condition is reported; no sweep from zero to all labels corrupted or test-error trend across corruption fractions.
No comparison of regularization or augmentation effects on fitting random labels or true-label generalization.
No result showing that real-label patterns are learned before noisy or random labels; the VoG distribution comparison does not measure learning order.
